findings.description: The reports bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored with S3-managed keys rather than a controlled KMS key; for an archive of reports this is missing encryption-at-rest configuration.

The bucket has neither an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block nor a restrictive bucket policy, and its ACL is not set to private, leaving it exposed to account-level defaults that could permit public access.
The ledger exports bucket, which holds financial ledger data, defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its contents are not encrypted with a customer-controlled KMS key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy is attached to this bucket containing ledger exports, so public access cannot be considered blocked.
The model artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored model artifacts are not encrypted under a controlled key.
No public access block or bucket policy is configured for the model artifacts bucket, leaving it to depend entirely on account-level settings to prevent public exposure.
The runbooks bucket stores operational documentation but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its objects are not encrypted at rest with a controlled KMS key.
No public access block or restrictive bucket policy is attached, so the runbooks bucket relies on unspecified account-level defaults for public access protection.

findings.issue_category: log delivery ACL on audit bucket
findings.description: The audit bucket is configured with acl = "log-delivery-write", which grants the S3 log delivery group write and ACL-read permission on this bucket; an audit trail bucket holding logs should deny server access logging writes to untrusted or broad principals rather than use a canned ACL.
Even though this bucket holds audit logs and uses KMS encryption, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy is defined to block public access.
The vendor roster object is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, a bucket with no explicit encryption configuration, so vendor data is stored without a controlled KMS key.
